source.title: DAGFormer: Global Topology Prediction for Transformer Cross-Layer Connections
source.authors: Xiao-Cong Yang; Yuren Hao; Cheng-Xiang Zhai

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures held-out language-model loss across model sizes and compute budgets and fits power laws, using an OLMo-2/Dolma setup rather than the original studies' setups. It does not test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports WikiText-2 loss measurements and parameter/compute fits. It also evaluates downstream tasks, but reports architecture comparisons rather than a test of downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss. The capacity controls do not isolate shape effects at fixed parameter count across a wide architecture range.
record.test_reason: The power-law fits (Section 4.1, Figure 2) are a tool for comparing DAGFormer with vanilla, not a test of the scaling law. The fit form L = E + A N^-α is assumed, not checked. The parameter fit uses three sizes (75M–300M, about 4×) per family with E shared, and no goodness of fit is reported. The 1B runs are below compute-optimal. No extrapolation, allocation, shape or downstream-predictability test is made. The vanilla numbers serve only as the comparator for the new architecture.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that DAGFormer lowers loss at every size from 75M to 1B and at equal compute. Its fitted exponents are larger, but they differ by about one standard error and nothing beyond 1B is tested.
record.recipe_differences: Scaling fits use matched OLMo-2 and DAGFormer models trained on Dolma; the routing cost is included in compute. The model-size fit shares the irreducible loss term between families, and the tested scale and training setup differ from the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted exponents differ between vanilla and DAGFormer; the compute fit includes routing cost, and the parameter fit omits 1B runs trained at the lower tokens-per-parameter budget.

fits_no_version.finding: With E shared, DAGFormer's fitted exponents exceed vanilla's: 0.56 vs 0.48 for parameters and 0.30 vs 0.27 for compute. The authors say the difference is about one standard error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-layer routing architectures change the fitted loss-scaling exponent relative to a standard Transformer.

record.problems: The largest model is 1B and is below its compute-optimal budget; most pretraining runs are single-seed. The authors say seed variation can make smaller loss differences noise, the two fitted exponents differ by about one standard error, and nothing beyond the largest run is tested. The parameter fit covers only 75M–300M; there is no independent prediction test or token-count fit.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Downstream-task and instruction-finetuning results are not extracted because they compare architectures and do not test downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss.

untested.parts: Whether loss actually follows a power law; parameter range is only 75M–300M; no token law; no check of fit quality.
No out-of-sample prediction of larger runs.
Only one width-or-depth capacity control at 75M/150M. This is a parameter-matched comparison, not a fixed-parameter shape sweep.
Downstream results are architecture comparisons, not a test of predictability from scale or loss.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' and its V1 supports/limits_scope labels are withdrawn. The scaling fits are used as an architecture-comparison tool, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The parameter sweep covers 75M–300M; the compute fit includes the reported runs up to 1B. The paper does not establish the law over several orders of magnitude, fit an independent token-count law, or test the stated condition that the other two factors are not bottlenecks.
No power law fitted on smaller runs is evaluated as an out-of-sample prediction of larger runs.
No sweep identifies loss-minimising parameter/token allocations at fixed compute or tests how either allocation scales with compute.
The capacity controls compare a few parameter-matched or near-matched vanilla and routed models; they do not isolate depth, width, or other shape effects over a wide range.
No scaling-law test is conducted in other modalities, on repeated data, or for fine-tuning or transfer.
Downstream results are reported as architecture comparisons, not as a test of predictable downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss.

The paper reports different fitted exponents for vanilla and DAGFormer, but does not systematically vary parameter counting, data, training schedule, or fitting method to test fit dependence or curve bending.
